public_rationale: He says the underlying economics "suggest" that no subscription AI service "makes any kind of financial sense." This is a hedged judgment, not a firm factual claim. It names no metric, no threshold, no set of services and no period. Turning it into a test of profitability or unit economics would supply terms he did not commit to, and reviewers flagged that as unfair. Companies also do not report AI subscription margins separately, so even a stricter reading would rest on estimates. I treat the claim as not adjudicable.
limitations: A firmer version of the claim (for example, that a named company's subscriptions lose money on a stated basis) could be checked separately.

He gives no metric, threshold, company set or period. "Financial sense" has no single plain reading: it could mean gross margin, contribution margin, operating profit or long-run viability.
The plain-reading rule is not applied to hedged language, so I do not convert this into a firm universal claim about profitability.
